cvEn:
Yosef (Yosi) Haiman, son of Nitza and Arie, was born on 26 Tevet 5708 (8 January 1947) in Sha'ar HaGolan. When he reached school age he attended the elementary school in Sha'ar HaGolan, and after finishing there he studied at the "Kinerot" institution in Beit Zera. At a young age he devoted himself to sport.

He belonged to the Hashomer Hatzair youth movement, and from the age of sixteen until his conscription into the IDF he was an instructor in the Hashomer Hatzair "ken" (branch) in Tiberias and Ramatayim. When he went to Tiberias he found paths to the hearts of young people; he understood them, cared for them, and invested all of himself in working for them, and they returned his love and admiration. He did not conduct his educational work in conventional ways, and he always sought new approaches.

In his last years he was interested in literature in general and in poetry in particular. After he fell, a notebook of his poems remained among his belongings, since for him poetry was a kind of diary, and in it he found expression for his loneliness and his personality.

A spirit of volunteering had stirred in his heart from childhood, throughout his years of service in the IDF, to which he was conscripted in July 1966. He began his path in a flight course, and afterward was an instructor for Nahal commanders. He served in the Military Police, but found no satisfaction in these roles. He aspired to take part in combat operations, and after efforts he volunteered to serve in the "Shaked" unit. However, while still serving his compulsory service, he was wounded in the course of carrying out his duties. For almost a month he wrestled with the angel of death, and on 22 Tishrei 5729 (14 October 1968) he died of his wounds. He was laid to rest in the cemetery in Sha'ar HaGolan. On the first anniversary of his fall, Kibbutz Sha'ar HaGolan published a booklet in his name and in his memory. The commander of his unit wrote to his parents in his letter of condolence, among other things: "I knew him only a short time, and I feel that in fact I have known Yosi for decades. Yosi symbolized for me the figure of a proud youth, a youth in whose heart burns attachment to our security problems, a youth who wants to be an inseparable part of these problems and among the pioneers who seek their solution."

Yosef is commemorated on the website "Shaked Unit Fighters Archive" at http://www.424shaked.co.il
